feeds.title: Middle-earth Blog
feeds.description: Middle-earth Blog is a repository of articles, news, and resources for fans of J.R.R. Tolkien's Middle-earth. It is a collection of essays about J.R.R. Tolkien and Middle-earth written by Michael Martinez from late 1999 to early 2003.

feeds.title: Tea with Tolkien Blog
feeds.description: Kaitlyn Facista is a Catholic convert, wife, mother to four babies at home + two in heaven, and a hobbit at heart. Her hope for the Tea with Tolkien blog is that it will be a source of encouragement and inspiration for anyone who loves Tolkien and wants to learn more about how his Catholic faith helped shape Middle-earth.

feeds.title: TheOneRing
feeds.description: Founded in 1999 by a group of like-minded Tolkien fans, TheOneRing.net continues today in bringing fans the latest news on the beloved figures involved in the making of the wildly popular Lord of the Rings movies as well as the newest information available on upcoming productions, Tolkien-centered events, new publications, and fan gatherings.

feeds.title: A Single Leaf Blog
feeds.description: A Single Leaf Blog covers articles on Tolkien studies, medievalism, old English, and university teaching - and sometimes all of those things all rolled up together. I'm Dr. Anna Smol, my blog posts aim to inform researchers in Tolkien studies as well as fans who are interested in exploring Tolkien's works and/or medieval literature.

feeds.title: Tolkien and Fantasy
feeds.description: Tolkien and Fantasy Blog is a musing on Tolkien and modern fantasy literature.

feeds.title: The Notion Club Papers
feeds.description: The Notion Club Papers (NCPs) Blog is an unfinished (posthumous) novel by JRR Tolkien. The Notion Club was a fantasy version of The Inklings.

feeds.title: Too Many Books and Never Enough
feeds.description: This is the weblog of Wayne G. Hammond and Christina Scull, husband and wife authors and book-collectors. They are well known as scholars concerned, in particular, but by no means exclusively, with the work of J.R.R. Tolkien, Arthur Ransome, and the artist Pauline Baynes.

feeds.title: Luke Shelton Blog
feeds.description: My name is Luke Shelton and I am a researcher who focuses on J.R.R. Tolkien, medievalism, and medieval texts. On this website, you will find information about my current research, my presentations and professional activities, and occasional random thoughts as well.

feeds.title: John Garth
feeds.description: I am the British author of the acclaimed biographical Tolkien and the Great War. I speak regularly on Tolkien and related topics and I have taught full-length and short courses on Tolkien for Oxford University's Department.

feeds.title: Parma-kenta
feeds.description: Enquiry into the books of Tolkien. Read thoughts on the works of J.R.R. Tolkien and related subjects.

feeds.title: A Tolkienist's Perspective
feeds.description: Hey, My name is James. This is a blog for fans of J.R.R. Tolkien, from complete beginners to avid enthusiasts, exploring the author's imaginary world, influential writing and cinematic adaptations.

feeds.title: Tolkien Britta
feeds.description: I'm Britta, a Tolkien collector, enthusiast, and aspiring scholar. I first ventured into Middle-earth via The Hobbit, which I read when I was eleven years old. I decided the best way to connect with other fans was to start blogging. Not long after I started that project, I became a reporter for the Middle-earth News, a Tolkien fansite which covers related literature, film, and gaming news.

feeds.title: The Tolkien Society Blog
feeds.description: Find the latest blog posts from Tolkien fans, artists, scholars and more.The Tolkien Society is an educational charity, literary society, and international fan club, devoted to promoting the life and works of J.R.R. Tolkien.

feeds.title: Dr Dimitra Fimi Blog
feeds.description: I am Dr Dimitra Fimi, senior lecturer in fantasy and children's literature, and a specialist in J.R.R. Tolkien and fantasy literature. Here you will find more information about my books, essays and articles, talks and lectures, and media appearances and contributions.
